problem: Visual RL agents for foraging/navigation overfit to training visuals and fail under held-out perturbations (fog, lighting), and it is unclear what architecture works best for behavioral robustness versus alignment with mouse neural activity.
motivation: Biological vision stays stable under visual variation while deep RL agents are brittle. The Mouse vs. AI competition tests both behavioral robustness (Track 1) and neural alignment (Track 2). The authors observed that complex architectures (InceptionNet, deep IMPALA ResNet, LSTM) overfit or failed to converge, which motivated testing simple designs.
key_idea: Use a tiny 2-layer CNN with GLU gating and observation normalization for robustness, and a deeper 16-conv ResNet+GLU for neural alignment, trained with PPO, with checkpoint selection around 200K steps.
insight: Depth hurts robustness: the 24-layer ResNet has a 30-point ASR-MSR gap (80.96 vs 51.00), while SimpleCNN has only a 2.8-point gap. Observation normalization is the main gain (+3.8 points in the ablation, 91.6→95.4 final score; GLU adds only +0.2). For neural alignment, more capacity helps (17.8M model ranks 1-6, the 1.4M SimpleCNN ranks 13), and alignment is non-monotonic in training steps (200K-step checkpoint rank 2 versus 520K-step checkpoint rank 6). Caveat: the alignment gaps are tiny (0.1517 vs 0.1451), and the ablation numbers come from single evaluations.
method: Track 1 encoder: Conv 8x8 s4 (16ch) and Conv 4x4 s2 (32ch) with LeakyReLU(0.2), flatten, FC to 256; 1.4M params in total.
GLU module (Track 1): parallel Swish feature path and sigmoid gate path (256-d), multiplied elementwise and projected back to 256, for selective feature filtering.
Observation normalization: running EMA mean/std normalization of the input, intended to give invariance to global illumination/contrast changes.

Track 2 encoder: 4x4 s4 stem (64ch), four stages 64→128→256→512 with 2x2 strided downsampling and 3x3 residual conv pairs (16 conv layers), then softmax-gated GLU layers and dense 256 projection; 17.87M params.

Training: PPO with Unity ML-Agents. Track 1 uses two phases: 1.4M steps for the backbone, then +350K steps after adding GLU. Track 2 saves checkpoints every 20K steps (60K-1.14M) and selects by leaderboard score.
Failed-approach study: InceptionNet, deep IMPALA ResNet, LSTM/SRU-LSTM and heavy data augmentation (weather, color jitter, masking) were all worse than the simple baseline.

setting.backbone: Two-layer CNN + GLU (Track 1) and 16-conv ResNet + GLU (Track 2), both trained from scratch with PPO
setting.training_data: Online RL in the competition Unity environment, no extra data; Track 1 uses 1.75M PPO steps in total; Track 2 uses 60K-1.14M steps
setting.action_space: Continuous 3D (forward/back velocity, lateral velocity, angular rotation rate)
setting.simulator: Unity (ML-Agents) Mouse vs. AI foraging environment

numbers.evidence: Table 1: Track 1 Visual Robustness results, SimpleCNN + GLU + Norm 96.80 / 94.00 / 95.40

numbers_note: Not a navigation-benchmark paper; results are on the Mouse vs. AI competition leaderboard, and the Track 2 score is reported as printed (rank lower is better).
results: Track 1: SimpleCNN+GLU+Norm reaches 95.4% final score, versus 87.7% for the IMPALA ResNet-4 baseline and 65.98% for ResNet-24. Track 2: the 17.8M ResNet+GLU reaches top-1 alignment (0.1517), ahead of the 1.4M SimpleCNN (0.1451, rank 13).
limitations: Task-specific and evaluated on a single competition environment, so generalization is untested.

Differences in the neural score are tiny, and there are no repeated seeds or confidence intervals; Track 2 ablations compare only against the Track 1 CNN, with no ablation of the deep model's components.
Some claims are hypotheses without verification (e.g., causes of non-monotonic training).
